'''Mariangiola Dezani-Ciancaglini''' (born 22 December 1946) is an Italian [[logic]]ian and [[theoretical computer science|theoretical computer scientist]] whose research topics include [[type theory]] and [[intersection type discipline]]s, [[lambda calculus]], and [[Semantics (computer science)|programming language semantics]]. She is a professor emerita at the [[University of Turin]].

==Education and career==
She was born on 22 December 1946 in Turin. After earning a master's degree in physics at the University of Turin in 1970, and working as a researcher in Turin as a [[National Research Council (Italy)|CNR]] fellow, she became an assistant professor of computer science at University of Turin in 1972, and full professor in 1981.{{r|ae}}

While continuing as a professor, she earned a Ph.D. from the [[Radboud University Nijmegen|Catholic University of Nijmegen]] in the Netherlands in 1996.{{r|ae}} Her dissertation, ''Logical Semantics for Concurrent Lambda-Calculus'', was jointly promoted by [[Henk Barendregt]] and [[Corrado Böhm]].{{r|mg}}

She served as dean of computer science at the University of Turin from 2005 to 2008, and retired to become a professor emerita in 2018.{{r|short}}

==Recognition==
She was elected to the [[Academia Europaea]] in 1993.{{r|ae}} In 2015 she was named a Fellow of the [[European Association for Theoretical Computer Science]] "for distinguished and seminal achievements in formal methods and foundations of programming languages, introducing or developing new type systems for the lambda-calculus as well as for the pi-calculus and related calculi".{{r|eatcs}}
